about.p1: Founded in 1963, the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda (CPR) is the umbrella body uniting Rwanda's 25 Protestant churches. items.title: CPR Staff Visit Nyanza Genocide Memorial and Support Survivor Families in Mulinja Village
items.excerpt: CPR staff paid tribute to victims at Nyanza Genocide Memorial in Kicukiro District and delivered targeted support to 1994 Genocide survivor families in Mulinja Village as part of annual Kwibuka 31 commemorations.
body: Conseil Protestant du Rwanda (CPR) is the Protestant Council of Churches in Rwanda. For over twelve (12) consecutive years, conducting annual Kwibuka commemoration activities—specifically visiting and supporting families of survivors of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi—has remained an established annual tradition within CPR.
On the occasion of Kwibuka 31, as Rwandans commemorate the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, CPR staff carried out two major key activities:
1. Visiting the Nyanza Genocide Memorial of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi in Nyanza, Kicukiro District, to pay solemn tribute to the victims.

2. Visiting and delivering support to families of survivors of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi resettled in Mulinja Village, Gahanga Sector, Kicukiro District. All of these commemorative activities were successfully conducted on 19 May 2025.

At the Nyanza Genocide Memorial, which is the final resting place for over 105,600 victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi from across Kigali City, CPR staff also visited the memorial gardens. They were guided through the deep symbolism embedded within the landscape features—such as sorghum fields, winding pathways, miniature hills, flowing water, papyrus reeds, and indigenous trees—learning the enduring lessons of memory, resilience, and unity today.

After visiting the memorial, CPR staff proceeded to visit families of Genocide survivors resettled in Mulinja Village. These 46 families have partnered with CPR and its staff in carrying out annual Kwibuka commemoration activities throughout the past 12+ years. Whenever resources allow, CPR visits these families to deliver essential support—including household supplies, food provisions, and other necessities.

On this occasion, CPR staff were joined by the General Secretary of CPR alongside the Representative of the CPR President. The delegation gathered at the Church of the Nazarene located near Gahanga Sector headquarters, meeting with all 46 survivor families resettled by Kicukiro District in Mulinja Village for a meaningful moment of fellowship, solidarity, and mutual encouragement.
items.quote: Remembering and standing alongside survivors is our continuous sacred duty. Through faith, memory, and practical support, we strengthen unity and hope.

items.title: Inside CPR's Annual Convention on Ecumenical Cooperation
items.excerpt: Rwanda's Protestant community is building sustainable partnerships across the country. Member churches met to align strategies for education, youth leadership, and socio-economic empowerment.
body: The 2026 Annual Convention of the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda brought together church leaders, theologians, and community champions from across East Africa to discuss the future of ecumenical partnership.
Keynote speakers highlighted the pivotal role of Protestant institutions in driving educational excellence, healthcare access, and environmental stewardship throughout Rwanda's provinces.

Bringing together more than 300 delegates, including ministers, ambassadors, development partners, academics, and youth leaders, the Convention marked the beginning of a long-term platform for advancing practical cooperation across member churches.
The convention concluded with a solemn declaration affirming mutual cooperation, interfaith dialogue, and active participation in national development projects.
items.quote: Ecumenical cooperation is not merely a theological goal—it is our active responsibility to serve humanity together.

items.title: CPR May 2026 Highlights & Youth Programs
items.excerpt: May 2026 was a landmark month for CPR's Youth Program, rolling out peacebuilding workshops and digital skills training for over 800 young church leaders nationwide.
body: Throughout May 2026, the CPR Youth Department conducted workshops across Western and Southern provinces, empowering young leaders with digital skills, conflict resolution tools, and entrepreneurship training.
Participants engaged in interactive seminars focused on digital evangelism, community service, and mental health awareness, preparing them to lead active initiatives within their parishes.
The success of the May youth initiatives sets the foundation for our upcoming national youth summit scheduled for later this year.
items.quote: Empowering young people with skills and faith is the highest investment we can make for Rwanda's future.

items.title: Kwibuka 31 Memorial Commemoration at Gahini Diocese
items.excerpt: CPR member churches joined thousands across Rwanda to remember the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, reaffirming their commitment to peace, reconciliation, and 'Never Again'.
body: As part of Kwibuka 31 commemorations, CPR leadership and member church heads gathered at the Gahini Diocese for a solemn memorial service honoring victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
Speakers stressed the continuous duty of Christian churches to promote truth, support survivors, and nurture genocide prevention education among younger generations.
CPR reaffirmed its pledge to support trauma healing clinics and community reconciliation dialogue groups throughout the country.
items.quote: Remembering is our sacred duty. Through memory, truth, and faith, we safeguard Rwanda's unity forever.

items.title: BNEP Launches Active Pedagogy Training for 1,200 Teachers
items.excerpt: The Bureau National de l'Éducation Protestante rolled out its flagship Participatory Active Pedagogy program in partnership with international development partners.
body: The Bureau National de l'Éducation Protestante (BNEP) officially launched an intensive training initiative for 1,200 primary and secondary school teachers serving in CPR-affiliated schools.
The program focuses on student-centered active learning, inclusive education for children with special needs, and integrating moral ethics into STEM curricula.
With over 595 schools managed by CPR member churches, BNEP continues to elevate educational standards across the nation.
items.quote: Quality education with strong moral grounding transforms learners into compassionate leaders.

items.title: Gender & Health Department Completes Trauma Counselor Certification
items.excerpt: Forty-two community health workers across five provinces were certified as trauma counselors, strengthening CPR's mental health outreach capacity.
body: CPR's Gender and Health Department celebrated the graduation of 42 certified community trauma counselors following a rigorous six-month practical training program.
These counselors are deployed across rural health centers and parish counseling desks to provide accessible psychosocial support, family mediation, and trauma care.
This initiative addresses mental health stigma and ensures compassionate care at the grass-roots level.
items.quote: Healing hearts and restoring mental well-being is vital for healthy families and strong communities.

items.title: CPR Partners with Local Cooperatives for Agricultural Sustainability
items.excerpt: A new initiative aiming to support rural communities with climate-smart farming techniques was launched in Eastern Province, impacting over 500 families.
body: CPR's Diakonia Department launched a climate-smart agriculture pilot project in collaboration with local farming cooperatives in Bugesera and Nyagatare districts.
The project equips smallholder farmers with drought-resistant seeds, drip irrigation kits, and organic soil management techniques to enhance food security.
Over 500 families have already benefited, increasing crop yields while conserving natural resources.
items.quote: Sustainable agriculture honors God's creation while securing livelihood and dignity for rural families.

items.title: Annual Youth Peace and Reconciliation Summit Announced
items.excerpt: Youth leaders from various Protestant parishes across the country will gather in Kigali to discuss peacemaking, leadership, and digital evangelism.
body: The CPR Youth Directorate has announced dates for the upcoming National Youth Summit, bringing together over 600 young representatives from Protestant churches nationwide.
Under the theme 'Youth as Ambassadors of Peace and Innovation', the summit will feature workshops on conflict resolution, social enterprise, and digital literacy.
Registration is open through local parish secretariats and CPR youth coordinators.
items.quote: When young people lead with peace and purpose, the entire nation moves forward.

radioPage.heroDesc: The official voice of the Protestant Council of Rwanda, reaching communities in every corner of the country with messages of faith, unity, and holistic development.
radioPage.introDesc: Radio Inkoramutima ("Voice of the Heart") is the official radio station of the Protestant Council of Rwanda. Born on 27 December 2012, the station broadcasts on 107.1 FM — uniting CPR member churches, spreading the Gospel, and promoting the holistic development and social welfare of Rwandan communities.

about.title: From a Long-Cherished Dream to Reality
about.desc: Many years before the Genocide against the Tutsi in 1994, the idea of a CPR radio kept returning in the discussions of CPR structural organ meetings — but it was never put into practice. The Ministry of Evangelism judged a radio communication tool relevant for spreading the Gospel to a great number of people across the country, the region, and the world.
body: At the beginning, CPR hired airspace on the national Radio Rwanda and started broadcasting evangelization messages for 30 minutes at a time.
CPR built a small studio at its head offices in Kicukiro, used by the Communication and Evangelization Department to prepare and edit evangelization programmes before they were aired on Radio Rwanda.

Protestant Sunday services were broadcast live by Radio Rwanda through two technical studios — one at the Saint Etienne cathedral of the Anglican Church of Rwanda (Diocese of Kigali) and the second at the Kiyovu parish of the Presbyterian Church.

In 2012, the CPR General Secretary, together with the Technical Staff team of the Mission and Church Mobilization Department and the support of radio technicians, conducted a study to establish Radio Inkoramutima.
On 27 December 2012, the dream of many years became a reality: Radio Inkoramutima was born.
Today the station operates 17 hours daily — from 5:00 am to 10:00 pm — from its premises at Kimihurura Sector, Gasabo District, Kigali.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.desc: Quick answers to the questions we hear most often.

items.q: How can my church become a member of CPR?
items.a: Membership is open to Protestant churches and Christian organizations in Rwanda that share our vision of unity and holistic development. Contact the General Secretariat and our team will guide you through the process.

items.q: How do I partner with CPR on a project?
items.a: We welcome national and international partners. Send us a message through the form or email partnerships inquiries to cprgs@cpr-rwanda.rw and our team will respond within 48 hours.

items.q: How can I support CPR's work?
items.a: You can support us through prayer, volunteering, or donations. Reach out to us and we will share the ways your contribution can make a lasting impact on Rwandan communities.

items.q: Can I request media coverage or an interview?
items.a: Absolutely. Our communications team handles media requests — including coverage of our events and interviews with our leadership. Contact us with the details of your request.

items.q: Where is the CPR head office located?

gs.title: General Secretary
gs.overview: The General Secretary's office provides overall leadership and strategic coordination for CPR, overseeing inter-church relations, institutional governance, and external partnerships. It serves as the central hub connecting all departments under a shared vision of faith, unity, and development.
keyActivities: Strategic planning and institutional governance
Coordination between member churches and departments
Representation at national and international forums
Management of inter-church dialogue and ecumenical partnerships
Oversight of CPR's organizational development initiatives

bnep.title: Education / BNEP
bnep.overview: The Bureau National de l'Enseignement Protestant (BNEP) manages and coordinates Protestant primary schools across Rwanda. With 595+ schools under its umbrella, BNEP focuses on quality education, teacher training, curriculum development, and school infrastructure improvements.
keyActivities: Management of 595+ Protestant primary schools nationwide
Teacher professional development and certification programs
Curriculum enhancement aligned with national education standards
School infrastructure improvement projects
Student welfare and scholarship programs
Monitoring and evaluation of education outcomes

diakonia.title: Diakonia / Development
diakonia.overview: The Diakonia department leads CPR's community development and psychosocial support programs. Rooted in faith-based service, it addresses trauma healing, reconciliation, and sustainable livelihoods through certified counselors, anti-trauma clubs, and church-community partnerships.
keyActivities: Psychotraumatology training and counselor certification
Anti-trauma clubs in schools and communities
Reconciliation and peace-building initiatives
Church-based community development programs
Support for vulnerable populations and social welfare
Partnership with ROPRE (Rwanda Organization of Psychotraumatology Experts)

finance.title: Finance & Mobilization
finance.overview: The Finance & Mobilization department ensures transparent financial management, donor relations, and resource mobilization for CPR's programs. With an AAA audit rating, it maintains the highest standards of accountability and fiduciary responsibility.
keyActivities: Financial planning, budgeting, and reporting
Donor relations and grant management
Resource mobilization and fundraising strategies
Internal and external audit coordination
Financial capacity building for member churches
Compliance with national and international financial standards

resources.title: Financial Transparency Report
resources.description: Annual financial statements and audit results

youth.title: Youth Program
youth.overview: The Youth Program department empowers young people across Rwanda through leadership training, annual summits, entrepreneurship programs, and faith-based mentoring. Reaching 10,000+ youth annually, it cultivates the next generation of community leaders.
keyActivities: Annual National Youth Summit organization
Leadership and entrepreneurship training camps
Faith-based youth mentoring programs
Youth advocacy and civic engagement initiatives
Inter-church youth exchange programs
Sports and cultural activities for youth development

resources.title: Youth Leadership Curriculum
resources.description: Training materials for youth development programs

gender.title: Gender Promotion
gender.overview: The Gender Promotion department advances gender equality and women's empowerment through GBV prevention training, women's cooperatives, economic empowerment programs, and advocacy for inclusive policies within churches and communities.
keyActivities: Gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response training
Women's economic empowerment through cooperatives
Gender mainstreaming in church and community programs
Advocacy for gender-responsive policies
Mentoring and leadership development for women
Community awareness campaigns on gender equality

resources.title: Women's Cooperative Handbook
resources.description: Guide for establishing and managing cooperatives

radio.title: Radio Inkoramutima
radio.overview: Radio Inkoramutima (107.1 FM) has been broadcasting hope and inspiration since 2005. As CPR's communications arm, the station reaches over 1 million daily listeners with faith-based programming, community news, educational content, and cultural programs.
keyActivities: Daily broadcasting of faith-based and community programming
News coverage and community reporting
Educational and health awareness programs
Cultural and music programming
Live event broadcasting for church activities
Digital media and online streaming expansion
